title: Local equation of one normalized Cartier Kummer representative
statement: Fix the finite coefficient setting P of [def-pur-conventions], with m=ell^n, A=P.Coefficient and n>=1. Let T be a separated finite-type k-scheme [sk-def-purity-conv], and i:D->T a closed immersion whose kernel ideal is invertible [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let kappa be a degree-two module Ext class from i_*A_D to the finite etale root line A(1), satisfying the relative torsor normalization SupportedKummerBoundary [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. For every etale e:U->T, global function f on U, and Cartesian square identifying D times_T U with V(f), the canonical pro-etale comparison of kappa, pulled back through this square in the supported-Hom model [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], is minus frameBoundary(f) [def-pur-frame-class]. It is also minus the one-factor ordered frameBoundaryProduct of the tuple Fin 1 -> Gamma(U,O), constantly f, after the exact singleton-support type identification. No finite-type or quasi-compact hypothesis is placed on e. The corresponding supported Hom representatives are supplied explicitly and identified with Ext.hom by HEq, so this is the same assertion without repeated derived-instance conversion.

proof.text: Use the canonical complementary frame of the dual ideal. The boundary witnesses and relative extension uniqueness identify its integral class; uniqueness of scalar realization identifies kappa with the framed realization. Pull back that framed pair along the chosen etale square.

On the principal chart e=f^-1 is a global frame and its complementary section is f e. The principal torsor Yoneda sign gives minus the Kummer localization boundary. The normalized relative-cone and root scalar/site comparisons identify this boundary with frameBoundary(f). This uses the specified relative extension, not an inference from local equality of ordinary degree-two classes.

For the singleton tuple the dependent left fold starts at the supported unit and appends this sole boundary. The supported cup unit law and canonical intersection/support comparison give the same class; Set.range_const identifies the supports. A unit equation and an empty chart give zero classes and require no exclusion.

theorem normalizedCartier_localEquation (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {D T : Scheme.{u}} (a : T ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    [IsSeparated a] [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a]
    (i : D ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hI : i.ker.IsInvertible)
    (κ : Abelian.Ext
      ((Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) i).obj (P.constantEtale D))
      (P.frameTwistEtale T 1) 2)
    (α : P.FunctorialCupH false i 2 1) (hα : HEq κ.hom α)
    (hκ : Etale.SupportedKummerBoundary P.Coefficient P.diagonalExponent
      P.diagonalExponent_annihilates i hI (P.diagonalExponent_isUnit a) κ)
    (U : Scheme.{u}) (e : U ⟶ T) [Etale e] (f : Γ(U, ⊤))
    (t : U.zeroLocusSubscheme {f} ⟶ D)
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare t (U.zeroLocusSubschemeι {f}) i e) :
    HEq (P.functorialCupPullback true i (U.zeroLocusSubschemeι {f}) e t sq
      a 2 1 (P.functorialCupCompare i 2 1 α))
      (-(P.frameBoundary U (e ≫ a) f)) ∧
    HEq (P.functorialCupPullback true i (U.zeroLocusSubschemeι {f}) e t sq
      a 2 1 (P.functorialCupCompare i 2 1 α))
      (-(P.frameBoundaryProduct U (e ≫ a) 1 (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ f)))
